content: Rifampin interacts with various drugs by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme metabolism, particularly through the CYP3A4 pathway. Below are the specific interactions and recommendations for monitoring or modifying therapy: 1. Quizartinib: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 2. Ranolazine: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or consider an alternative drug. 3. Repaglinide: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Repotrectinib: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Resmetirom: Rifampin increases its levels or effects through other mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. 6. Revefenacin: Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Ribociclib: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inducers. 8. Rifabutin: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Rifampin and Pyrazinamide: Combined use increases hepatotoxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Rimegepant: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Abiraterone: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If unavoidable, increase abiraterone dosage frequency to twice daily. 12. Alfentanil: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Alfuzosin: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects through CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Alosetron: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Aluminum Hydroxide: Concomitant use reduces rifampin absorption. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before antacids. 16. Magnesium Carbonate/Trisilicate: Similar to aluminum hydroxide, these antacids reduce rifampin absorption. Administer rifampin 1 hour before antacids. 17. Ambrisentan: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Amikacin: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Amitriptyline: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP2C19, CYP3A4 metabolism, and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Amlodipine: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects through CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Amobarbital: Rifampin decreases its levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Antipyrine: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Apalutamide: Rifampin levels are reduced due to increased elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Armodafinil: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Artesunate: Rifampin reduces its active metabolite (DHA) levels by inducing UGT. Monitor for decreased efficacy. 26. Asenapine: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Atogepant: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 28. Atorvastatin: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Atovaquone: Rifampin reduces its levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Avanafil: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor response carefully in patients with erectile dysfunction. 31. Avatrombopag: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 32. Azithromycin: Increases rifampin levels via P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Rifampin reduces their levels or effects via P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Belumosudil: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Increase the dosage to 200 mg twice daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A inducers. 35. Bendamustine: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Benzhydrocodone/Acetaminophen: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for withdrawal or respiratory depression when discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers. 37. Berotralstat: Rifampin reduces its levels via P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitor or titrate P-gp substrate dose if coadministered. 38. Bexagliflozin: Rifampin decreases its levels via UGT1A9 metabolism. Consider adding another antihyperglycemic agent for additional glycemic control. 39. Bexarotene: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Bortezomib: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Bosentan: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Bosutinib: Increases rifampin levels via P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Brentuximab Vedotin: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Brexpiprazole: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Double the dose over 1–2 weeks if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 45. Brivaracetam: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP2C19 metabolism. Increase the dose up to 100% when coadministered. 46. Bromocriptine: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Budesonide: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Buprenorphine: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for withdrawal symptoms and adjust dosage as needed. 49. Bupropion: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Butabarbital: Rifampin reduces its levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Cabazitaxel: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 52. Calcifediol: Rifampin reduces its half-life by stimulating microsomal hydroxylation. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 53. Calcitriol: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Calcium Carbonate: Reduces rifampin absorption. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before antacids. 55. Canagliflozin: Rifampin reduces its levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Cannabidiol: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 57. Carvedilol: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Caspofungin: Rifampin decreases its levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Cenobamate: Rifampin reduces its levels via CYP2B6 metabolism. Increase the dose of CYP2B6 substrates as needed. 60. Cevimeline: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Chlordiazepoxide: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Chloroquine: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Cholic Acid: Rifampin increases its toxicity by decreasing elimination. Monitor liver function tests and avoid inhibitors of bile salt efflux pumps. 64. Citalopram: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 65. Clarithromycin: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Clomipramine: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 67. Clonazepam: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Clorazepate: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 69. Clotrimazole: Increases rifampin levels through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 70. Clozapine: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 71. Conjugated Estrogens: Rifampin reduces their levels or effects via P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 72. Cortisone: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 73. Crizotinib: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 74. Cyclophosphamide: Rifampin decreases its levels or effects via CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 75. Cyclosporine: Rifampin reduces its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Modify therapy and monitor closely. This list highlights the importance of monitoring drug interactions with rifampin, as it significantly alters the metabolism and efficacy of many medications.
